tools.name: get_reward_discrepancies
tools.description: USE THIS whenever a customer questions or disputes their cash back / rewards and you need to find which specific transactions were rewarded incorrectly. First call get_credit_card_transactions_by_user to retrieve their transactions, then call this tool passing those transactions as clean JSON. It returns the transaction_ids whose recorded reward does NOT match the expected reward under Rho-Bank policy (it derives the correct per-card rate and does the arithmetic for you). Do the reward math with this tool — do not eyeball it yourself.

params.transactions:
JSON array. For EACH transaction include ONLY these raw fields, normalized to plain values:
- transaction_id (string), transaction_amount (NUMBER, e.g. 126.36 — strip any currency symbol), rewards_earned (NUMBER, e.g. 126 — strip any unit word), transaction_date (MM/DD/YYYY)
- credit_card_type, merchant_name, category — copied from the transaction record
- account_open (MM/DD/YYYY) — the opening date of the account that card belongs to, copied EXACTLY from the account record you fetched (do NOT guess it from transaction dates)
★Do NOT look up, reason about, or provide reward RATES, promos, or any computed value — a separate deterministic system reads the reward-rate policy and computes the expected reward itself.
params.account_open: OPTIONAL. Normally leave this empty and put account_open inside each transaction row instead. Use this argument ONLY when you pass 'transactions' by "@last:" reference: then pass this too as "@last:<the tool whose output contains the account records>" and the deterministic system fills each row's account_open by exact record match.

examples: get_reward_discrepancies(transactions=[{"transaction_id":"txn_ab12","transaction_amount":175.00,"rewards_earned":175,"credit_card_type":"EcoCard","category":"Green"},{"transaction_id":"txn_cd34","transaction_amount":320.00,"rewards_earned":775,"credit_card_type":"Gold Rewards Card","category":"Shopping"}])  -> returns the transaction_ids with a reward discrepancy that need a cash back dispute

isolate.instructions:
You determine cash-back reward rates by reading this bank's reward-rate policy documents.
FIRST search the knowledge base for the reward-rate policy of EACH card below — including its exceptions/exclusions — using the search tool. Search before you answer; do not answer from memory.
Then, for EACH item, report ONLY these values, read from the policy documents:
- base_rate: the base cash-back rate that applies to THIS item, as a percent number (e.g. 10 for 10%, 4 for 4%, 0 if this item earns nothing). It depends on the card, the purchase category, the merchant (policies may exclude specific merchants), and how long a subscription has run.
- promo_mult, promo_window_months, promo_start, promo_end: if a limited-time promo (e.g. double cash back for new customers) exists for this card, its multiplier, window length in months, and the promo period dates (MM/DD/YYYY). If no promo exists, use promo_mult=1 and empty dates.
★Do NOT compute the final rate, do NOT apply the promo, do NOT multiply, and do NOT judge whether the promo dates apply — a deterministic system does all of that. Report only what the documents say.
★Cards often list DIFFERENT rates per purchase category (e.g. a boosted rate for some categories and a base rate for everything else). For each item you MUST use the rate matching THAT item's category, quoting the category-specific rate line — quoting the base-rate line for a boosted-category purchase is the most common error and silently hides real discrepancies. If you cannot find a documented rate for an item, answer null for that item's base_rate instead of guessing — a wrong rate is worse than an unverified row.

operand_schema.promo_mult: <promo multiplier e.g. 2 for double, or 1 if no promo>
operand_schema.exclusion_policy_merchant: <if you downgraded this item because the policy EXCLUDES this specific merchant: the merchant name EXACTLY and COMPLETELY as the policy text names it, copied verbatim from your exclusion_quote — copy the WHOLE name the policy uses (e.g. 'Target'), never a fragment of it. Empty otherwise>
operand_schema.exclusion_pin_kind: <'named_merchant' if the exclusion sentence names this specific merchant; 'category' if it excludes a TYPE of merchant or purchase (e.g. 'General Retailers', 'Gaming Subscription Merchants') and you judged this item to belong to that type; empty if no exclusion applies>

isolate.inject_instructions:
You are a bank rewards specialist. Below are ALL policy documents for the {group}, then the customer's transactions on that card. For EACH transaction report:
- base_rate: the cash-back RATE that applies to THIS transaction (percent number: e.g. 10, 5, 4, 1, or 0 if it truly earns nothing). This is the rate the documents assign to this transaction's CATEGORY and MERCHANT — it may be an ELEVATED/bonus rate (when the card gives a higher rate for that category) or the standard rate.
  ★If the documents give a HIGHER rate for this transaction's category, APPLY that higher rate. Do NOT fall back to the standard/base rate just because you are unsure whether the merchant qualifies — downgrade to the standard rate ONLY when a document EXPLICITLY names this specific merchant in an exclusion list, and then copy that exact excluding sentence into 'exclusion_quote' (else leave empty).
  ★★The transaction's 'category' field is the bank's OWN authoritative classification of that purchase — treat it as final. If a category qualifies for a bonus rate, apply that bonus rate to EVERY transaction in that category. Do NOT second-guess an individual transaction using how many merchants you think are 'partners', how large the partner network is, or whether YOU personally recognize the merchant — the bank has already classified it. The ONLY thing that lowers the rate is an explicit merchant name in an exclusion list.
  ★Do NOT return 0 just because a purchase is not a premium/bonus category — almost every card earns a base rate on all other purchases; apply it.
- promo_mult, promo_window_months, promo_start, promo_end: if a limited-time promo (e.g. double cash back for new customers) exists for this card, its multiplier, window length in months, and the promo period dates (MM/DD/YYYY). If no promo, use promo_mult=1, promo_window_months=0, empty dates.

{docs}

tools.name: check_rebate_qualification
tools.description: ALWAYS provide user_id/credit_card_account_id (so the tool can verify against the records itself). USE THIS to determine whether a customer qualifies for a spend-threshold annual fee rebate (e.g. the Platinum Rewards Card annual fee rebate). Do NOT eyeball the monthly totals yourself. First read the customer's transactions and their card account opening date, and look up the required monthly spending threshold from the knowledge base, then call this tool. It buckets every transaction into the anniversary-based monthly windows of the cardmember year (by posting date, from the opening date), sums each window, and returns QUALIFIES only if EVERY window meets the threshold (a single month below disqualifies; no proration). Call get_current_time first and pass today's date as as_of_date - the tool evaluates the last complete cardmember year as of that date.

It computes, from the documented per-class fee schedules, each class's out-of-network ATM fee total and foreign ATM fee total for that usage (documented monthly free allowances deducted). It does NOT rank or pick a class - compare the returned totals yourself against what the customer asked to minimize, check the candidate class's other documented terms (eligibility, minimum deposits, monthly fees) in its source docs, and confirm the choice with the customer. Do the fee math with this tool - do not eyeball it yourself.

params.months: number - how many months the customer's usage pattern covers (their stated trip/usage duration).
params.withdrawals_per_month: number - the customer's stated ATM withdrawals per month.
params.withdrawal_amount: number - the customer's stated typical amount per withdrawal in USD (no $).
